newsitem.title: INDIA: Buyers drive India sugar up despite low arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Buyers drive India sugar up despite low arrivals.

text.p: Sugar prices lifted further on the local market on Wednesday as fresh consumer buying dragged prices upwards though limited arrivals kept offerings at a low ebb, dealers said.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 5 rupees at 1,430/1,465 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 rose by the same margin at 1,470/1,500 rupees per quintal.
"Arrivals of sugar from local mills to the Bombay market remained slow due to increased outstation buying at the mill level coupled with limited offerings by millers," a broker said.
"Local millers are witnessing increased buying from Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and southern states," he said.
Sugar mill delivery climbed up to 1,360/1,375 rupees per quintal from 1,355/1,365 rupees per quintal on higher outstation buying at the mill level.

Local millers who expect to get higher prices in coming days are offering a limited quantity of sugar at the current level which in turn has curtailed arrivals in the Bombay market. Overall market sentiment was firm at the close of the session.
